Chapter 22 · Topic 1

Mole concept + stoichiometry

Physical Chemistry Mixed Concepts - Advanced MasterSurface, Nuclear & MasteryTopic 1 of 20

Explanation

Concept. In Physical Chemistry Mixed Concepts - Advanced Master, Mole concept + stoichiometry: mole-plus-stoichiometry chains counting into balanced recipes. Mole is the chemist counting unit: one mole contains \(N_A = 6.022 \times 10^{23}\) entities, and links mass, number and volume through \(n = m/M = N/N_A = V/22.4\,L\) at STP.
Key formula(s). \[ n=m/M,\;n_1/\nu_1=n_2/\nu_2 \]
Key points.
  • Number of entities \(=\) moles \(\times N_A\); never multiply grams directly by \(N_A\).
  • For mixtures, total moles \(=\) sum of component moles; average molar mass \(=\) total mass/total moles.
  • JEE trap: STP volume applies only to gases, never to liquids or solids.
  • Always convert every quantity to moles first, then use the balanced-equation mole ratio.
  • At STP one mole of any gas occupies \(22.4\,L\); at NTP the same value is used in JEE.
Example 1.

How many moles and molecules are present in \(9\,g\) of water?

  1. Molar mass of \(H_2O = 18\,g\,mol^{-1}\), so \(n = 9/18 = 0.5\,mol\).
  2. Molecules \(= 0.5 \times 6.022\times10^{23} = 3.011\times10^{23}\).
  3. Atoms \(= 3 \times 3.011\times10^{23} = 9.03\times10^{23}\) since each water has 3 atoms.

Answer: \(0.5\,mol\), \(3.011\times10^{23}\) molecules.

Example 2 (JEE pattern).

(JEE pattern) A mixture of \(CH_4\) and \(C_2H_6\) weighing \(8\,g\) occupies \(5.6\,L\) at STP. Find the mole fraction of \(CH_4\).

  1. Total moles \(= 5.6/22.4 = 0.25\,mol\); let \(x =\) moles of \(CH_4\).
  2. Mass: \(16x + 30(0.25-x) = 8 \Rightarrow 16x + 7.5 - 30x = 8 \Rightarrow x = -0.5/-14\), solving gives \(x \approx 0.036\,mol\).
  3. Mole fraction \(= 0.036/0.25 \approx 0.143\).

Answer: About \(0.14\) (solve mass + mole equations simultaneously).

Common mistakes / JEE traps.
  • Using \(22.4\,L\) for non-gaseous substances.
  • Forgetting to multiply by atomicity when asked for atoms.
  • Mixing average molar mass with mole fraction weighting.

Chapter 22 · Topic 4

Thermodynamics + equilibrium

Physical Chemistry Mixed Concepts - Advanced MasterSurface, Nuclear & MasteryTopic 4 of 20

Explanation

Concept. In Physical Chemistry Mixed Concepts - Advanced Master, Thermodynamics + equilibrium: thermo-plus-equilibrium chains Delta-G into K. Advanced problems chain two chapters: convert units to moles first, apply the first law, then feed its output (e.g. \(K\), \(E\), \(pH\)) into the second. Integer-answer (0-999) and multi-correct formats reward checking limiting cases and dimensions at each link.
Key formula(s). \[ \Delta G^\circ=-RT\ln K,\;K=e^{-\Delta G^\circ/RT} \]
Key points.
  • Phase change: \(\Delta S = \Delta H_{trans}/T_{trans}\) (equilibrium temperature).
  • Multi-correct: test each option independently; assertion-reasoning needs the REASON to explain the assertion, not merely be true.
  • Roadmap first: write both governing equations before substituting numbers.
  • Entropy of mixing: \(\Delta S_{mix} = -R\sum n_i\ln\chi_i > 0\) always.
Example 1.

(Graph) A first-order \(\ln k\) vs \(1/T\) plot has slope \(-6000\,K\). Find \(E_a\) in \(kJ/mol\) (nearest integer).

  1. Slope \(= -E_a/R\).
  2. \(E_a = 6000\times8.314 = 49.9\,kJ \approx 50\).

Answer: \(50\).

Example 2 (JEE pattern).

(Multi-correct) Which plots are linear for first order: (A) \([A]\)-\(t\), (B) \(\ln[A]\)-\(t\), (C) \(1/[A]\)-\(t\)?

  1. Only \(\ln[A]\) vs \(t\) is linear.
  2. (B) only.

Answer: (B) only.

Common mistakes / JEE traps.
  • Breaking the chain (using raw data in step 2 without step-1 conversion).
  • Rounding integer answers early (keep 4+ digits till the end).

Chapter 22 · Topic 5

Thermodynamics + electrochemistry

Physical Chemistry Mixed Concepts - Advanced MasterSurface, Nuclear & MasteryTopic 5 of 20

Explanation

Concept. In Physical Chemistry Mixed Concepts - Advanced Master, Thermodynamics + electrochemistry: thermo-plus-electro chains heat into cell charge. Advanced problems chain two chapters: convert units to moles first, apply the first law, then feed its output (e.g. \(K\), \(E\), \(pH\)) into the second. Integer-answer (0-999) and multi-correct formats reward checking limiting cases and dimensions at each link.
Key formula(s). \[ \Delta G^\circ=-nFE^\circ_{cell} \]
Key points.
  • Roadmap first: write both governing equations before substituting numbers.
  • Entropy of mixing: \(\Delta S_{mix} = -R\sum n_i\ln\chi_i > 0\) always.
  • Phase change: \(\Delta S = \Delta H_{trans}/T_{trans}\) (equilibrium temperature).
  • Multi-correct: test each option independently; assertion-reasoning needs the REASON to explain the assertion, not merely be true.
Example 1.

(Multi-step) \(2\,mol\) ideal gas expands isothermally (\(300\,K\), \(5\to15\,L\)), then the heat absorbed drives electrolysis (\(n = 2\)). Find moles of metal deposited if all heat became electrical work at \(1.1\,V\).

  1. Heat \(= -w = nRT\ln3 = 2\times8.314\times300\times1.0986 \approx 5483\,J\).
  2. Charge \(= 5483/1.1 \approx 4985\,C\); moles \(e^- = 4985/96485 \approx 0.0517\); metal \(= 0.0258\,mol\).

Answer: About \(0.026\,mol\) (illustrates chaining).

Example 2 (JEE pattern).

(JEE Advanced pattern) \(\Delta H_{vap} = 40\,kJ/mol\) at \(373\,K\). Find \(\Delta S_{vap}\) and comment (Trouton).

  1. \(\Delta S = 40000/373 \approx 107\,J\,mol^{-1}K^{-1}\).
  2. Near Trouton constant (\(\approx 85\)-\(88\)); higher value hints at hydrogen bonding.

Answer: About \(107\,J\,mol^{-1}K^{-1}\).

Common mistakes / JEE traps.
  • Breaking the chain (using raw data in step 2 without step-1 conversion).
  • Rounding integer answers early (keep 4+ digits till the end).

Concept. In Physical Chemistry Mixed Concepts - Advanced Master, Kinetics + thermodynamics: kinetics-plus-thermo separates how fast from how far. Advanced problems chain two chapters: convert units to moles first, apply the first law, then feed its output (e.g. \(K\), \(E\), \(pH\)) into the second. Integer-answer (0-999) and multi-correct formats reward checking limiting cases and dimensions at each link.
Key formula(s). \[ k=Ae^{-E_a/RT},\;\Delta G=\Delta H-T\Delta S \]
Key points.
  • Entropy of mixing: \(\Delta S_{mix} = -R\sum n_i\ln\chi_i > 0\) always.
  • Phase change: \(\Delta S = \Delta H_{trans}/T_{trans}\) (equilibrium temperature).
  • Multi-correct: test each option independently; assertion-reasoning needs the REASON to explain the assertion, not merely be true.
  • Roadmap first: write both governing equations before substituting numbers.
Example 1.

(Multi-step) \(0.5\,mol\,CaCO_3\) decomposes; the \(CO_2\) is bubbled into lime water giving \(x\,g\) precipitate. Find \(x\).

  1. \(CO_2 = 0.5\,mol\); \(Ca(OH)_2 + CO_2 \to CaCO_3 + H_2O\).
  2. Precipitate \(= 0.5\times100 = 50\,g\).

Answer: \(50\).

Example 2 (JEE pattern).

(JEE Advanced) pH of \(10^{-3}\,M\,Ba(OH)_2\)? Give \(100\times(pH-10)\) as integer.

  1. \([OH^-] = 2\times10^{-3}\); \(pOH = 2.70\); \(pH = 11.30\).
  2. \(100\times1.30 = 130\).

Answer: \(130\).

Common mistakes / JEE traps.
  • Breaking the chain (using raw data in step 2 without step-1 conversion).
  • Rounding integer answers early (keep 4+ digits till the end).

Chapter 22 · Topic 11

Redox + electrochemistry

Physical Chemistry Mixed Concepts - Advanced MasterSurface, Nuclear & MasteryTopic 11 of 20

Explanation

Concept. In Physical Chemistry Mixed Concepts - Advanced Master, Redox + electrochemistry: redox plus electrochemistry links the exchanged electrons to cell charge through Faraday law. Advanced problems chain two chapters: convert units to moles first, apply the first law, then feed its output (e.g. \(K\), \(E\), \(pH\)) into the second. Integer-answer (0-999) and multi-correct formats reward checking limiting cases and dimensions at each link.
Key formula(s). \[ w=MIt/nF\;from\;n\,e^- \]
Key points.
  • Roadmap first: write both governing equations before substituting numbers.
  • Entropy of mixing: \(\Delta S_{mix} = -R\sum n_i\ln\chi_i > 0\) always.
  • Phase change: \(\Delta S = \Delta H_{trans}/T_{trans}\) (equilibrium temperature).
  • Multi-correct: test each option independently; assertion-reasoning needs the REASON to explain the assertion, not merely be true.
Example 1.

(Multi-step) \(2\,mol\) ideal gas expands isothermally (\(300\,K\), \(5\to15\,L\)), then the heat absorbed drives electrolysis (\(n = 2\)). Find moles of metal deposited if all heat became electrical work at \(1.1\,V\).

  1. Heat \(= -w = nRT\ln3 = 2\times8.314\times300\times1.0986 \approx 5483\,J\).
  2. Charge \(= 5483/1.1 \approx 4985\,C\); moles \(e^- = 4985/96485 \approx 0.0517\); metal \(= 0.0258\,mol\).

Answer: About \(0.026\,mol\) (illustrates chaining).

Example 2 (JEE pattern).

(JEE Advanced pattern) \(\Delta H_{vap} = 40\,kJ/mol\) at \(373\,K\). Find \(\Delta S_{vap}\) and comment (Trouton).

  1. \(\Delta S = 40000/373 \approx 107\,J\,mol^{-1}K^{-1}\).
  2. Near Trouton constant (\(\approx 85\)-\(88\)); higher value hints at hydrogen bonding.

Answer: About \(107\,J\,mol^{-1}K^{-1}\).

Common mistakes / JEE traps.
  • Breaking the chain (using raw data in step 2 without step-1 conversion).
  • Rounding integer answers early (keep 4+ digits till the end).
